text:
Noah Chen: Heads up — MediBridge opened a ticket on renewal invoice 99213, they say an HSM line was charged twice and a platform promo was applied twice.
Aisha Gupta: Can you drop the invoice snippet here? I haven't pulled it yet.
Noah Chen: Snip:
```
Invoice 99213 (renewal)
- Private deployment license: $60,000
- Platform fee (annual): $10,000
- Platform promo credit: -$1,500
- Platform promo credit (duplicate): -$1,500  <-- extra credit
- HSM managed key add-on: $3,200
- HSM managed key add-on (duplicate): $3,200  <-- duplicate charge
- Support (Premium): $15,000
Total: $87,400
```
BillingBot: (automated) Received dispute for invoice 99213. Running duplicate-line detection and credit memo history. Found: duplicate HSM charge and duplicate platform promo credit created during legacy->billing-v2 migration. Creating case BLG-2026-412.
Aisha Gupta: Interesting mix — one is an overcharge (HSM) and one is an over-credit (promo). We should net them rather than two separate refunds if customer prefers credit to next invoice.
Revenue Ops - Sam: For renewals we usually offer credit note applied to next billing period unless the customer requests refund. We need approval to issue CN-5601 and/or refund $1,700. Put it on the ledger.
SRE - Lina: FYI metering confirms only one HSM usage event in logs. Duplicate line is definitely a billing import artifact.
Legal - Omar: Clause check: standard renewal terms allow us to correct billing errors and issue credit notes. Recommend sending a short explanatory statement that avoids admitting systemic negligence. Keep it factual.
Noah Chen: Proposed math: duplicate HSM = +$3,200 credit to customer; duplicate promo = -$1,500 extra credit to customer, so net credit from us = $1,700. We can either (A) issue credit note CN-5601 for $1,700, or (B) issue full HSM credit CN-5602 for $3,200 and reverse the extra promo memo. Any ops preference?
Aisha Gupta: Option A cleaner for the customer (single line). But some accounts insist on line-item parity. Ask MediBridge preference in the ticket.
Revenue Ops - Sam: Approve CN-5601 for $1,700 to be applied to next invoice. If customer requests refund, finance will issue via ACH — flag for approvals.
BillingBot: (automated) Credit note CN-5601 queued for creation. Case BLG-2026-412 updated.
Legal - Omar: Agree with wording: "We discovered an internal billing duplication affecting your renewal invoice and have issued a corrective credit note for $1,700. Attached is the corrected invoice and credit note. Please tell us if you prefer a cash refund instead of applying the credit to your next invoice." Minimal liability language ok.
Noah Chen: I'll reply in ticket with that text and ask refund vs credit preference. Also add that invoice PDF will be reissued.
Aisha Gupta: After customer confirms, can Billing/Revenue Ops process CN and either apply it or refund. Sam, please confirm funds flow.
Revenue Ops - Sam: Confirmed. If refund requested, route to finance-payments with case BLG-2026-412 and tag "refund-approval". If credit applied, we'll consume CN on the next renewal invoice.
SRE - Lina: I'll add a backlog ticket for Billing Eng to add a guard in migration scripts to dedupe credit memos by external_memo_id. Filed as ENG-BILL-148.
Noah Chen: Thanks team. I'll post the customer reply here and then we can close BLG-2026-412.
BillingBot: (automated) CN-5601 created (pending application). Notifying revenue ops and updating case.
Noah Chen: MediBridge replied, prefers credit to next invoice. I'll mark case resolved after CN is applied. Closing plan: apply CN-5601, reissue corrected invoice PDF, notify customer with the approved wording."
